title: Leser-Trelat sign: eruptive seborrheic keratoses (internal malignancy)
vignette: A 65-year-old man comes to the office due to fatigue, decreased appetite, and weight loss. He has lost 5.4 kg (12 lb) over the last 3 months and eats only small portions of food because he feels full soon after he begins eating. The patient smokes a pack of cigarettes per day and drinks alcohol socially. Blood pressure is 152/90 mm Hg and pulse is 90/min. Physical examination shows a firm, 3-cm lymph node above the left clavicle. Numerous skin lesions are seen on the patient's trunk (multiple pigmented, well-demarcated, greasy 'stuck-on' plaques), as shown; the lesions were not present during his last physical examination 1 year ago. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient's skin lesions?

clues.text: feels full soon after he begins eating
clues.note: Early satiety with weight loss in an older smoker raises concern for gastric (or other GI) malignancy.

clues.text: firm, 3-cm lymph node above the left clavicle
clues.note: A left supraclavicular (Virchow) node signals metastatic abdominal/GI malignancy - here likely gastric adenocarcinoma.
Pigmented, waxy, well-demarcated 'stuck-on' plaques are seborrheic keratoses.

clues.text: the lesions were not present during his last physical examination 1 year ago
clues.note: ABRUPT eruption of numerous seborrheic keratoses is the Leser-Trelat sign - a paraneoplastic marker of internal (often GI) malignancy.

whatMatters: Numerous pigmented, greasy, 'stuck-on' plaques = SEBORRHEIC KERATOSES. Their SUDDEN eruption (Leser-Trelat sign) in a patient with weight loss, early satiety, and a Virchow node is a paraneoplastic marker of internal malignancy (gastric adenocarcinoma). Answer E.
strategy: Identify seborrheic keratoses by their classic 'stuck-on,' waxy, well-demarcated pigmented appearance, then recognize the eruptive (Leser-Trelat) context signaling occult malignancy. Reject melanoma (single asymmetric lesion with irregular borders/color change), neurofibromatosis (soft neurofibromas + cafe-au-lait/childhood onset), psoriasis (silvery-scaled plaques on extensors), acanthosis nigricans (velvety flexural hyperpigmentation), and tuberous sclerosis (hypopigmented macules, angiofibromas - a childhood neurocutaneous syndrome).

eliminations.label: Acanthosis nigricans - velvety flexural hyperpigmentation
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: velvety, hyperpigmented thickening of flexural skin (neck/axillae), linked to insulin resistance (and, as a paraneoplastic sign, GI malignancy). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it's a diffuse velvety plaque in flexures, not discrete 'stuck-on' keratoses on the trunk. ✅ Correct if: velvety axillary/neck hyperpigmentation.

eliminations.label: Malignant melanoma - single asymmetric changing lesion
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a malignant melanocytic lesion (ABCDE: asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this is MULTIPLE monotonous, greasy stuck-on lesions - typical of seborrheic keratoses, not a single evolving melanoma. ✅ Correct if: one asymmetric, multicolored, changing lesion.

eliminations.label: Neurofibromatosis - soft neurofibromas, childhood onset
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: soft, mobile neurofibromas with cafe-au-lait macules/axillary freckling (NF1). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: those are soft flesh-colored tumors from childhood, not pigmented greasy keratoses erupting at 65. ✅ Correct if: neurofibromas + cafe-au-lait + Lisch nodules.

eliminations.label: Psoriasis - silvery-scaled extensor plaques
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale on extensor surfaces/scalp. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: psoriasis has silvery scale (Auspitz sign), not greasy 'stuck-on' pigmented keratoses. ✅ Correct if: scaly extensor plaques.

eliminations.label: Tuberous sclerosis - neurocutaneous syndrome (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an inherited neurocutaneous disorder with hypopigmented (ash-leaf) macules, facial angiofibromas, shagreen patches, and periungual fibromas. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it presents in childhood with different skin findings and seizures, not eruptive seborrheic keratoses in an older adult. ✅ Correct if: ash-leaf macules + angiofibromas + seizures/tubers.

reasoning: Multiple pigmented, greasy, well-demarcated 'stuck-on' plaques = seborrheic keratoses
Their SUDDEN eruption (not present a year ago) = Leser-Trelat sign
Occurs paraneoplastically with internal malignancy (weight loss, early satiety, Virchow node = gastric adenocarcinoma)
mechanism: Seborrheic keratoses are benign epidermal proliferations appearing as sharply demarcated, waxy or greasy, pigmented papules/plaques with a characteristic 'stuck-on' look; they are extremely common in older adults and usually accumulate slowly. The abrupt, ERUPTIVE onset of numerous seborrheic keratoses is the LESER-TRELAT SIGN, a paraneoplastic phenomenon thought to result from tumor-secreted growth factors/cytokines (e.g., transforming growth factor-alpha, epidermal growth factor); it is most associated with GASTROINTESTINAL adenocarcinomas (classically gastric). This patient's weight loss, early satiety, and left supraclavicular (Virchow) node point to gastric adenocarcinoma, and the sudden crop of seborrheic keratoses fits Leser-Trelat. (Acanthosis nigricans can arise via the same paraneoplastic mechanism.) The distractors are distinguished by morphology and demographics: melanoma (a single evolving, irregular lesion), neurofibromatosis and tuberous sclerosis (inherited neurocutaneous syndromes of childhood), psoriasis (silvery-scaled plaques), and acanthosis nigricans (velvety flexural hyperpigmentation).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Derm > seborrheic keratosis: benign 'stuck-on' greasy pigmented plaques; eruptive onset = Leser-Trelat sign (paraneoplastic, GI/gastric adenocarcinoma); acanthosis nigricans similar mechanism.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: 'Stuck-on' pigmented plaques erupting suddenly = seborrheic keratoses (Leser-Trelat) -> look for internal malignancy.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on seborrheic keratosis, 'stuck-on'/greasy plaque, Leser-Trelat sign, Virchow node, or paraneoplastic? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Melanoma (single evolving lesion), neurofibromatosis/tuberous sclerosis (childhood neurocutaneous), psoriasis (silvery scale), acanthosis nigricans (velvety flexural).

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the trunk photo: numerous discrete, pigmented, waxy, well-demarcated plaques with a 'stuck-on' appearance. Anchor: 'stuck-on greasy plaques = seborrheic keratoses; sudden crop = Leser-Trelat.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: eruptive seborrheic keratoses (Leser-Trelat) -> internal malignancy (gastric adenocarcinoma); Virchow node = metastatic GI cancer.
